title: Self-Enumeration for Phase II of Census 2027 Commences in Goa, Punjab, Uttar Pradesh and Non-Snow-Bound Areas of Uttarakhand
subtitle:

body_text: The Self-Enumeration (SE) process for Phase II of Census 2027 i.e. Population Enumeration (PE) has commenced today in the States of Goa, Punjab, Uttar Pradesh and the non-snow-bound areas of Uttarakhand. Residents can submit their household details online till November 30, 2026. The corresponding house-to-house Population Enumeration in these States and areas will be conducted from December 1, 2026 to January 4, 2027 followed by a revisional round from January 5 to 9, 2027. The reference date for these States/areas will be 00:00 hours of January 5, 2027. In the remaining States and Union Territories, Population Enumeration will be conducted from January 25 to February 28, 2027 followed by a revisional round from March 1 to 5, 2027. The provision for Self-Enumeration in these States/UTs will be available from January 10 to 24, 2027, prior to the commencement of house-to-house visits by Enumerators. The reference date for Census in these States/UTs will be 00:00 hours of March 1, 2027. The Houselisting and Housing Census (HLO) under Phase I of Census 2027 have been completed across 35 States and Union Territories, except Manipur, marking the completion of first phase of the Census exercise. For the first time, Census 2027 is being conducted using digital tools, with Self-Enumeration introduced as an additional facility. It is a secure, convenient and user-friendly web-based facility available in 16 Indian languages. To participate in Self-Enumeration during Phase II, residents can log in to the official portal se.census.gov.in using their mobile number (preferably the one registered during Phase I) along with basic details and answer 40 notified questions covering household and individual particulars. Upon successful submission, a unique Self-Enumeration ID (SE ID) is generated, which is to be shared with the Enumerator during the subsequent field visit to complete the process. While Self-Enumeration allows residents to provide their details online at their convenience, Enumerators will continue to carry out door-to-door visits in all allocated blocks. Households that do not opt for Self-Enumeration will be covered during the house-to-house visits by Enumerators. All information collected under the Census Act, 1948, remains strictly confidential and is used solely for statistical purposes and development planning. Residents are encouraged to actively participate in this important national exercise and extend their cooperation to Enumerators. **** RK/RR/SK/PR/PS
